Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 2 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 7 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 0 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes
Some rules and regulations set by local leaders are limiting us to have power and freedom to make decisions in our life as youth.

We are excluded from programs taking place in this community such as the Presidential Input Scheme yet some of us are farmers. If we ask local leaders they say, “The programs are for parents [older people] not youth.” As youth [who are farmers], lack of agriculture inputs is limiting us to make major decision on farming activities.
Most of us are under the authority of our parents who dictate what we should do in life.
We are not able to marry many wives because of the rules set by our parents. We do not have land permits/offer letters, which are limit us on what we can do with the agricultural land.
The youth who are on step 4 are those who have lost their parents. They are free to do whatever they want in their life because they do not have someone who is controlling them.
Going to school is important because education is the key to success in life. Without education life would be difficult.
Going to school equips us with knowledge which we can use in our day-to-day lives and to have direction in life.
When you are educated, you will have many job opportunities throughout your life and you can easily get a job that you aspire to do.
Being educated is important because the Zimbabwe of today needs someone who is well educated to get by easily in life.
Even for one to be successful in farming, one needs knowledge we gain from school.
Education is important because you can easily update yourself with technology.
Most boys finish school at form 4 while girls finish at form 2.

Our parents show same commitment in educating their daughters as their sons but the only problem is lack of money to pay school fees. When there is shortage of fees, our parents opt for the boy to proceed over the girl. They say that a boy child shall be the household head responsible for the up keep of children and his wife.
Some parents do not care about sending a girl child to school; they see it as a waste of money because she is going to leave the family when she gets married.
Parents say the person who shall marry their daughters will be responsible for her life so there is no need of sending their daughters to school.

Improved varieties
Young men in XX prefer short season varieties

These short season varieties give small yield but they early maturity is what we want. Because they mature early, you quickly do away with hunger. Women prefer open pollinated varieties (OPVs) because they matures early while men prefer new improved hybrid varieties because they give high yield.
The area under maize production is declining because of input shortages.
Maize production has declined because people have ventured into tobacco and soya bean production.
We are selling our maize to Grain Marketing Board and traders.
The quantity of maize being sold has declined; those who sell more sell about 4 tonnes and the smallest amount sold is 0.5 tonnes.
OPVs are good because they require relatively less fertiliser and are drought resistant.

More yields are harvested from a small piece of land cultivated.
There is low level of fertilizer leaching.
Efficient use of fertilizer since it is applied per planting station.
The plants grow vigorously.
It saves money because you plant a small plot yet yielding more.
It conserves the soil which will be used by the next generation. Mulch applied in the field conserves moisture.

Trees gives us oxygen.
Forest conservation results in soil conservation by preventing soil erosion. Most of the things we use in our day-to-day lives come from the forest.
It conserves pasture for our livestock.

These changes have nothing to do with changes in weather patterns/climate variability. The availability of markets for the crops has caused these changes. Farmers need to raise money to sustain their livelihoods. In 2004 cotton had a good market and prices were also good. One could therefore grow cotton, sell it and then buy maize grain for food. Maize is now important because cotton prices have fallen. One can easily do barter trade with maize on essential commodities such as salt, sugar and cooking oil.
Maize is the main crop grown by people because it is the staple crop.
Tobacco and soya beans are cash crops.
Sheep production has decreased because they are easily affected by diseases.

In 2004 there was a rule which did not allow people to keep goats in the resettlement area. They were a problem animal because they preferred feeding on tree saplings, yet the goal was to protect and conserve our forests. Generally, a goat is a naughty animal. However, if one tethered their goats at the homestead, they could keep goats. Hence, gradually people started keeping goats.

Goats are mostly used in cultural practices like paying lobola. We were also facing problems in meeting certain lobola obligations that demanded payment in the form of a goat. At first people paid the cash equivalent of a goat but people started complaining that were abandoning our culture because what was traditionally needed was a live goat. As a result we had to travel long distances to buy live goats for marriage rites. Because of such problems we were finally allowed to keep goats.
There are no differences.
Even a girl child can now grow maize for sale. There is no problem with that because she is just looking for cash.
Tobacco and soya beans she can grow because everyone needs money.

Young women do not want to grow tobacco because of high labor needs. In addition, it is not easy for a young woman to grow tobacco because people will talk a lot of bad things about the young women. They will think that her growing of tobacco is because she is being used by her family in some occultist practices. This discourages young women from growing tobacco in this community. But if she has a big piece of land under sweet potatoes and the crop is looking good everyone will say XX is a young women of virtue, because that is a woman’s crop.

It is not possible for young women to keep many cattle that they acquire themselves. I would not allow that to happen in my home. However, young women can keep many cattle if they inherit them from the parents, as what happens when the young woman is the eldest surviving child upon the death of the parents. Even in that case, the brothers to the young woman’s [late] father will find ways of disposing of the cattle. For example, they will ask the young woman for a bigger ox to sell because the one belonging to the brother is not big enough to fetch a good price. When it comes to replacing the ox they will give the young woman wardrobe instead, as the equivalent of the price of the ox.

Women cannot keep cattle. Even if the husband offers her cattle she will refuse because raising cattle demands a lot of labour. It is not easy for a women to go and herd cattle in the pastures. But if you offer a woman a cow or ox to sell and keep the money she will quickly accept that, because selling is easy [laughter]. However, the woman will still consult the man on what price to charge and what to do, or what she wants to do, with the money from the sale of cattle.

It is easy for young men to raise livestock such as chickens for themselves because they will be trained to be the father in future but on selling it will be decided by him and the parents. The difficult they might face is lack of initial capital.

In a household people use one plot together, there are no cases whereby some members of the household have their own plot. In cases where some household members are responsible for some plots, such in polygamous households, the land is distributed according to the quality of soil. Men usually take soils with good quality because they are responsible for growing crops for the family.
A man will help his wife in ploughing the fields only.
A woman works on her husband’s plot frequently because that is where the food for the family is grown.
Men will hire additional labor and pay with money or maize grain.
Young men do not have other responsibility that interferes with farming responsibilities.
[In general, is the right kind of labor available for agricultural activities when needed?] There is shortage of labour for agricultural activities.
[How do [men] obtain additional labor when needed - in or outside the household?] Men will hire additional labor and pay with money or maize grain.
How do female-headed households go about obtaining adult male labor when they need it during the rainy season?]
They hire adult male labor and pay with maize grain or money. Some employ young men who work full time at the woman’s home, doing the tasks that men should do.
If she has cattle, she will collaborate with a man without cattle and assist each other in most farming activities.
The woman will consult her husband; if she is a single woman she will consult her parents.
